issues.t: CVT slipping, hesitating or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs but the car is slow to pick up speed, it hesitates at stoplights, the transmission whines or rattles, or the car stops moving altogether.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission (CVT) is the Cube's most reported problem. Owners describe failures at around 80,000-100,000 miles, and some cars needed a new transmission much earlier. Wrong or old CVT fluid makes failure more likely.
issues.next: Change the CVT fluid with genuine Nissan NS-2 fluid on schedule. If it slips or whines, get a diagnosis right away and ask Nissan whether any extended CVT coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: CVT surging or not holding a steady speed
issues.sym: The car surges or shudders at a steady speed, the tachometer moves up and down on its own, or it struggles to hold speed on the highway.
issues.why: Nissan released a service bulletin (NTB11-016) with a software update for this kind of surging. In some cars it was an early sign of internal CVT wear.
issues.next: Ask a Nissan dealer to check for the transmission computer update. If surging continues after the update, have the CVT inspected.

issues.t: Electronic steering lock fails and the car won't start
issues.sym: The steering wheel stays locked, the push-button start does nothing or flashes a warning, and the car cannot be driven, often at home or in a parking lot.
issues.why: The electronic steering column lock (ESCL) unit fails on many early Cubes. It is the most reported steering complaint for 2009 and 2010 and the second most common repair in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have it towed to a shop or dealer. Ask Nissan whether any warranty extension covers the steering lock on your VIN before paying, and keep your receipts.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem only shows up if the driver airbag deploys.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator can separate from the steering wheel when the airbag fires, which can injure the driver. Nissan recalled more than 50,000 Cubes in 2026 after a federal investigation.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall R26A1 (NHTSA 26V-230). The dealer checks the inflator serial number and replaces it if needed, free of charge.

issues.t: Fuel can leak and create a fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: A fuel system defect on some early Cubes could let fuel leak, which could start a fire near an ignition source.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and get it checked. Confirm the free recall repair (NHTSA 10V-330) was done.

issues.t: Tire can lose air from a tire pressure system defect (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light comes on and a tire goes flat at a steady rate.
issues.why: Nissan recalled 2009 Cubes over a defect in the tire pressure monitoring system parts that can let a tire leak air until it is flat. Owners also report split valve stems on these cars.
issues.next: Never ignore the tire pressure light. Check your VIN for recall 09V-393 and have the tire sensors and valve stems inspected.

issues.t: Start/stop button can stick and shut off the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving after going over bumps, and the start button may feel stuck.
issues.why: The engine start/stop button can catch in its housing. Road vibration can then press it and turn the engine off.
issues.next: Confirm the free recall repair (NHTSA 15V-418) was done. If the engine shuts off while driving, steer to safety; you will lose power assist.

issues.t: Exhaust flex joint or muffler rusts and breaks
issues.sym: A loud exhaust, a rattle or drone from under the car, or exhaust fumes you can smell.
issues.why: The exhaust flex joint, pipes and muffler connections rust and crack. They are among the most common repairs owners report.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected on a lift. Fix leaks quickly so fumes cannot get into the cabin.

issues.t: Catalytic converter failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with a catalyst code, a rotten egg smell, sluggish acceleration or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Owners report failed catalytic converters on these Cubes, sometimes after misfires or oxygen sensor faults.
issues.next: Fix any misfire or bad oxygen sensor first, then have the converter tested. Check whether the federal emissions warranty still covers it.

issues.t: Brake light switch failure stops the car from starting
issues.sym: The engine will not start with the push button, the brake lights stay off or stay on, or warning lights appear.
issues.why: The push-button start needs a signal from the brake pedal switch. When the switch fails, the car thinks your foot is not on the brake.
issues.next: Ask someone to check the brake lights while you press the pedal. A new brake light switch is cheap and quick to fit.

issues.t: Rattle or vibration at idle from worn engine mounts
issues.sym: A rattle or vibration when the car comes to a stop after warming up, or a clunk when pulling away.
issues.why: Engine and torque rod mounts wear or crack, and some were not installed correctly from the factory.
issues.next: Have the engine mounts and torque rod bushings inspected. Replacing a worn mount is usually a modest repair.

issues.t: Check engine light with a mass airflow code
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0101, sometimes with hesitation or poor fuel economy.
issues.why: A dirty or failing mass airflow (MAF) sensor, or in some cases engine computer software, can trigger the code.
issues.next: Try cleaning the MAF sensor with the proper spray first. If the code returns, ask a dealer about a software update before replacing the sensor.

issues.t: Rear door won't open from the latch or remote
issues.sym: The side-hinged rear door will not open with the button, key or remote.
issues.why: The rear door latch actuator can fail, and dirt and corrosion in the latch can make it stick.
issues.next: Use the emergency release from inside if needed. Lubricating the latch can help; a failed actuator needs replacement.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cargo area
issues.sym: Damp carpet, water stains or a musty smell in the cargo area behind the rear seat.
issues.why: Dirt builds up on the rear door weather seals so they stop sealing flush, and damaged seal segments let water in.
issues.next: Clean and inspect the rear door seals. Replace any cracked or flattened sections and dry the carpet to stop mold.

issues.t: Humming from a worn wheel bearing
issues.sym: A hum or growl that rises with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs wear out and are one of the more common repairs owners report.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked on a lift. A badly worn bearing can overheat, so do not wait too long.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The gauge never shows full, drops too fast, or jumps around on hills. A check engine light may come on.
issues.why: Faulty fuel level sending units were reported repeatedly by owners. Some cars needed the sender or fuel tank parts replaced more than once.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you do not run dry. Have the sending unit tested if the gauge is unreliable.

issues.t: Fuel door latch breaks
issues.sym: The fuel door will not open or close, or a piece of the latch snaps off.
issues.why: Part of the fuel door latch mechanism is fragile and can break.
issues.next: The repair means removing the wheel well liner to reach the latch. It is not a hard job for a shop or a handy owner.

issues.t: Airbag light on and horn stops working
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The spiral cable (clock spring) behind the steering wheel can break its connections. It carries the airbag, horn and steering wheel controls.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. A failed clock spring means the driver airbag may not deploy, so fix it soon.

issues.t: Heater blower grinds or only works on some speeds
issues.sym: A grinding noise from behind the dash when the fan runs, the fan only works on high, or weak airflow.
issues.why: Leaves and debris can get into the blower fan, and the blower motor resistor can burn out.
issues.next: Have the cabin air filter and blower checked. Clearing debris or replacing the resistor or motor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Check engine light from an EVAP vent valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with EVAP codes such as P1421 or P0448, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: The evaporative emissions vent control valve can fail, and some cars also needed the engine computer reprogrammed.
issues.next: Check that the gas cap is tight, then have the EVAP system tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: Oil leak from the timing chain cover
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the engine or oily residue on the side of the engine.
issues.why: Owners report the sealant on the timing chain cover leaking on some Cubes.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. Have the source confirmed, since resealing the timing cover is a big labor job and a shop may suggest monitoring a slow seep.

issues.t: Power window switch fails
issues.sym: A window will not move from the driver's switch or works only some of the time.
issues.why: The power window switch contacts wear or get dirty. Owners report replacing the master switch assembly.
issues.next: Try the window from its own door switch to narrow it down. A shop can clean or replace the switch.
